sexual activity and use of cloth during menstruation are important risk factors for the initial episode of UTI in Indian women.

the risk factors for first and recurrent UTI among Indian women are: Anal sex, short interval between sexual intercourse, use of cloth during menstruation, high tea consumption, vaginal infections, back to front wiping, history of UTIs in first-degree female relatives, constipation and stress incontinency.

women with first-time cystitis had a higher risk of infection if they had a history of anal sex, if they had a shorter interval between the last sexual intercourse and the current infection, if they consumed more than 250 ml of tea daily, if they wiped from back to front, if they had an infection of vagina and if they used a cloth during menstruation.
